problem.claim: Learn scalable computational methods for sampling from Boltzmann distributions when the target is specified only through an unnormalized energy function.

gap.claim: Without explicit target samples, prior diffusion samplers often require importance-weighted estimation or complicated learning procedures, with scalability limited by extensive energy and model evaluations.

contributions.claim: Proposes Adjoint Schrödinger Bridge Sampler (ASBS), using matching-based objectives without estimating target samples during training.
Provides an adjoint-matching perspective from stochastic optimal control for scaling Schrödinger Bridge diffusion samplers and states a convergence proof to the global solution.
Extends recent Adjoint Sampling to arbitrary source distributions by relaxing its memoryless condition.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize ASBS as a new diffusion sampler combining simple, scalable matching objectives with Schrödinger Bridge structure and no target-sample estimation during training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on classical energy functions, amortized conformer generation, and molecular Boltzmann distributions.
The authors report demonstrating that Schrödinger Bridge-based diffusion samplers can be learned at scale through Adjoint Matching and proving convergence to the global solution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Boltzmann sampling is considered when only an unnormalized energy function is available.
Prior diffusion samplers may need importance weighting or complicated learning, while extensive evaluations limit scalability and practical use.
ASBS is introduced with target-sample-free matching objectives and Schrödinger Bridge grounding.
Adjoint Matching is framed through stochastic optimal control, with a stated global-convergence result and generalization to arbitrary source distributions.
The method is reported across classical, conformer-generation, and molecular Boltzmann sampling tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a practical training constraint—no explicit target samples—to a matching-based objective, then separately states theoretical grounding and convergence.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes the method’s motivation, mechanism, and claimed guarantee easier to trace.
lessons.application: When introducing a method for sample-scarce learning, explicitly map the data constraint to the training objective and state any supporting theory as a distinct claim.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the objective or theoretical result is not actually established for the proposed method.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, baselines, datasets, compute costs, or experimental conditions.
The convergence statement does not specify assumptions, the exact notion of convergence, or whether it applies to all practical implementations.
The abstract does not detail how ASBS differs algorithmically from Adjoint Sampling beyond relaxing the memoryless condition.
